meta.title: MTB3A — Log it before you forget it

hero.subheadline: Every client, every payment, every expense — captured in seconds on your phone, visible instantly in your hosted portal. Built for growing businesses that move fast.
hero.altNote: Accounts are set up for your organization — there's no public sign-up.
hero.altNoteOpen: Sign up with your email address, or ask us to set an account up for your organization.

clients.title: Every client on one page.
clients.body: What you did for them, what they owe right now, and when they last paid — together on one page, with nothing to dig for.

payment.title: Paid? Two taps.
payment.body: Tap {action} next to what they paid for. The amount left and today's date are already filled in — tap once more and it's recorded.

businesses.title: Every business you run.
businesses.body: Give each business its own profile, with its own clients and numbers, and switch between them in one click. Dollars, shekels and euros stay apart — never quietly added together.

privacy.title: Your records, on every device you sign in on.
privacy.body: An MTB3A account keeps everything behind your sign-in — the same numbers on your phone and in the portal, backed up every day and restorable to any point in the last week.

phone.title: Log it on your phone. See it all in your hosted account.
phone.body: The phone app is for logging: an income or an expense in seconds, even with no signal. The portal, your hosted account in a browser, is where you see it all: every client, what they owe and what they’ve paid, on any computer.
phone.hint: Both come with the same account.
phone.devicesCaption: Logged on the phone, there in the portal.

malafat.title: Run a law firm or accounting office on Malafat? MTB3A connects to it.
malafat.body: Malafat keeps each firm's fee proposals and agreements, and what every client owes and has paid. Link your firm's Malafat to your account, and a payment you log in the MTB3A phone app reaches Malafat under its client, unallocated, for the firm to apply to what's owed.

faq.headline: Questions
faq.a1: No — accounts are set up for your organization, with pricing based on what you need. Request an account and we'll reply with an offer.
faq.a1Open: No. You can create an account with your email address, or request one and we'll reply with an offer for your organization.
faq.a2: On MTB3A's servers, behind your sign-in — not only on one device. We back up every day and can restore your records to any point in the last 7 days.
faq.q3: How do I back up, or move to another device?
faq.a3: Nothing to do — your account is the backup. Sign in on a new device and everything you've logged is already there.
faq.q4: Can I track more than one business?
faq.a4: Yes. Give each business its own profile, with its own clients and income, and switch between them in one click.
faq.a5: {currencies}. Each amount keeps the currency it was earned in, and totals are shown per currency — never converted behind your back.
faq.q6: Does it work offline, or on my phone?
faq.a6: The hosted portal works in any browser — sign in and your records are there. The phone app is built for offline capture: log an expense with no signal, and it uploads the moment you're back online.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.intro: This policy covers MTB3A's website, its hosted web portal and its iPhone and Android apps. The portal and the apps work the same way: you sign in with an account, and what you enter is saved to MTB3A's servers. It does not cover any other product.

scope.title: The short version
scope.body: MTB3A is a hosted product. You sign in with an account, and what you enter — clients, projects, income, expenses, receipts — is saved to our servers so it's there on every device you sign in on. Our website sends us what you type in the account-request form, only if you fill it in and press Send, and it counts visits anonymously, as described under "Anonymous usage counts". Each visit to its home page also asks our servers whether sign-up is open, as described under "What reaches the network". None of our apps use ads or tracking, and we never sell your data.

mobile.title: iPhone and Android: your account and our servers
mobile.body: The mobile apps need an account. While sign-up is open you can create one yourself on the hosted portal, as described under "When you create an account"; otherwise your organization or we set one up for you. When you sign in, we keep your email address, display name, language, and which business profiles you can use. What you enter is stored on MTB3A's servers, and a copy is kept on your phone so the app works offline. Entries you make while offline are saved on your phone and uploaded once you're back online. Signing out ends your session on our servers. Entries that haven't uploaded yet stay on the phone and upload after you sign in again.

hostedAccounts.title: Where your records live
hostedAccounts.body: Your account (the web portal, and the iPhone and Android apps when you're signed in) keeps your records on MTB3A's servers in Google Cloud's me-west1 region, and our daily backups stay there too. We keep each backup for 14 days, and we can restore your records to any moment in the last 7 days. Google Cloud encrypts your records, receipts and backups where they are stored, and our servers reach the database only over encrypted connections. Our servers' technical logs are kept by Google Cloud for 30 days, and may be stored outside the me-west1 region. With your account we also keep, for each place you're signed in, a shortened description of your browser or app (never your IP address); for each passkey you add, its public key and identifier, never your fingerprint or face; and for each email we send you, a scrambled form of your address and whether it arrived, for 30 days. MTB3A is run by a small team, and the people who run it can technically reach your data. We look at your records only when you ask us to help, to fix a fault, or when the law requires it, and changes made with our admin tools are logged. Error reports go to Sentry in the EU, as described under "Error reports". Usage counts from the portal and the apps go to PostHog in the EU only if you agree; our website counts visits anonymously, as described under "Anonymous usage counts". What happens when you close your account is described under "Deleting your account and data". Accounts are also covered by our terms of service.

createAccount.title: When you create an account
createAccount.body: While sign-up is open, you can create an account yourself on the hosted portal. You type your email address and we email you a link that works for 24 hours; your account is created only when you open that link and set a password. Until then we keep only your address and the page's language with the link, and we delete them about a week after the link expires. The sign-up and password-recovery forms first run a check with Cloudflare Turnstile to tell people from bots. Turnstile receives your IP address and details about your browser and device, and never what you type into the form. To check that your address can receive email, our servers look up its domain (the part after the @) in public DNS records, and ask the domain's registry, through its public registration records (RDAP), when the domain was registered. Only the domain name is sent in these lookups, never the rest of your address. We don't accept addresses from disposable email services or at domains that can't receive email. Sign-ups from personal email providers or email-forwarding services, and from domains these lookups can't confirm (for example, one registered in the last 90 days), are reviewed by our team before the account opens; we keep the domain and the reason for the review with it, and we email you the outcome.

email.title: Emails we send
email.body: We email you only about your account: the link to finish creating it or to set a new password, a reminder that you already have an account if you try to sign up again, a notice when your password changes or a passkey is added to your account, a notice that we're reviewing your sign-up and then its outcome, notices that your free trial is ending, that your account has become read-only, or that it will lock, and, when you close your account, a notice with the day it will be deleted. Our emails never include amounts or your records, and we don't track whether you open them or click their links. We send them through Resend, which receives your email address, the message and what happens to it (for example, that it was delivered or bounced). Resend sends our emails from the EU (Ireland) and keeps its records of them, including your email address and their delivery, in the United States, under its data processing agreement with us. If an email to you bounces permanently or you mark it as spam, we stop emailing that address, and we keep the address on our do-not-email list so it stays that way.

whatYouEnter.title: What you enter
whatYouEnter.body: You control what goes into MTB3A: client names and contact details, projects, income records, optional expenses, notes, and any receipts you attach. It's sent to our servers so it can be stored with your account. On iPhone, you can share a photo or PDF of a receipt into MTB3A. It's uploaded to private cloud storage and attached to the expense. Receipts you upload may be read automatically on MTB3A's own servers, to suggest the amount, date, currency and vendor. The reading is done by software we run ourselves: no outside AI or OCR company ever sees your receipts, and no AI language model reads them. We don't keep the text read from a receipt, only the suggested fields, and you review them before you save the expense.

network.title: What reaches the network
network.body: The website's account-request form sends what you type in it to Netlify when you press Send. Each time you open the website's home page, it asks our servers whether sign-up is open. That request carries nothing about you, but like any request it reaches our servers with your IP address and browser details, which go into the technical logs described under "No ads, no tracking". The website also sends the error reports described under "Error reports" to Sentry and the anonymous visit counts described under "Anonymous usage counts" to PostHog. The hosted portal connects to MTB3A's servers and, if you turned on anonymous usage, to PostHog. The hosted portal also sends the error reports described under "Error reports" to Sentry, and its sign-up and password-recovery pages connect to Cloudflare Turnstile for the check described under "When you create an account". The mobile apps connect to MTB3A's servers, to Sentry for error reports, to the private storage that holds your receipts, and, if you turned on anonymous usage, to PostHog, always over encrypted connections.

sharing.title: Who else handles your data
sharing.body: We don't sell your data or share it with advertisers. Our servers and receipt storage run on Google Cloud, which processes the data only to host it for us. When a receipt is read to suggest its fields, our own software does it on those servers, so no other company reads it. Cloudflare carries the connections between you and our hosted portal and servers, and runs the Turnstile check described under "When you create an account". Resend sends our emails, as described under "Emails we send". Stripe handles payments: when you subscribe, it receives your name, your email address and a random internal ID for your account, and you type your card and billing details on Stripe's own checkout page, so they never reach our servers. Sentry, hosted in the EU, receives the error reports described under "Error reports" and stores them for us. Our website runs on Netlify, which receives the account-request form and checks each request for spam with Akismet (made by Automattic). PostHog, hosted in the EU, processes the anonymous usage counts described under "Anonymous usage counts" for us. Emails you send to info@mtb3a.com are kept by Microsoft, which hosts our mailbox. Business profiles we set up for an organization that uses Malafat share their records with Malafat; profiles you create yourself never do. Beyond that, we disclose data only when the law requires it.

security.title: Keeping the mobile apps secure
security.body: Your password is stored on our servers only as a secure hash, and never on your phone. Your sign-in session is kept in the iPhone Keychain or in Android's encrypted storage. On your phone, the app's records are protected by your phone's own encryption, and from version 0.1.13 they're left out of iCloud and Google backups. You can turn on App Lock so opening the app needs Face ID, Touch ID, your fingerprint, or your device passcode. That check happens on your device, and MTB3A never receives your biometric data. The mobile apps don't use your camera, contacts, or location, and they only see a photo or file when you choose to share it into the app.

noTracking.title: No ads, no tracking
noTracking.body: None of MTB3A's apps use advertising or tracking that follows you across sites or apps. Our website, our servers, the hosted portal, and the iPhone and Android apps send error reports when something breaks, as described under "Error reports". The anonymous usage counts we do keep are described under "Anonymous usage counts". Our servers keep technical logs for 30 days (when a request arrived, what it asked for, and whether it succeeded) so we can run the service. Our own log lines never include your IP address. Google Cloud's record of each request includes the address that connected, which is usually Cloudflare's rather than yours. Our servers use your IP address only briefly, in memory, to slow down repeated attempts such as wrong passwords, and pass it to Cloudflare Turnstile for the check described under "When you create an account". We don't use any of this to profile you.

usageAnalytics.title: Anonymous usage counts
usageAnalytics.body: Where we count usage, we use PostHog, hosted in the EU. We never send amounts, names, notes, contact details, your location, or anything you type, and nothing we send is linked to your account. Our website counts page visits and which buttons are pressed, without cookies and without storing anything on your device. With each count it sends the page's address, the page you came from, any campaign tags in the link (such as utm_source), and whether you're on a computer, tablet or phone. To tell visits apart for a single day, PostHog combines your IP address and browser details into a code that changes every day and keeps neither, so a visit can't be linked to you or to visits on other days. The hosted portal asks you once whether you want to share anonymous usage, and it's off unless you turn it on. If you do, it sends a short note when you turn it on (saying whether you did so from the prompt or the account menu), each time you open the portal, each time you save an income, an expense or a payment received, and when it shows the free trial's reminder to add a card and whether you chose to add one or not. A note says only which of these it was, its currency, for an income whether it was already paid, and for the trial reminder whether it showed when you first signed in or on your Home page, along with the portal's version and its analytics library's version, its language, your browser's type, your device's operating system and its version, and whether it's a computer, tablet, or phone. Notes are sent under a random ID kept only in your browser, not linked to your account, and replaced when you sign out. If you turn it off from the account menu, we send one last note saying you turned it off, then stop and delete the random ID. The iPhone and Android apps ask you once whether you want to share anonymous usage, and it's off unless you turn it on. If you do, they send a short note each time you turn it on (saying whether you did so from the prompt or Settings), once more the first time you turn it on after signing in, and each time you add a client or save an income or an expense. A note says only which of these it was, its currency, and for an income whether it was already paid, along with the app's version and its analytics library's version, its language, your phone's operating system and its version, and whether it's a phone or a tablet. Notes are sent under a random ID kept only on your phone, not linked to your account, and replaced when you sign out. If you turn it off in Settings, we send one last note saying you turned it off, then stop and delete the random ID. These counts are used only to understand which parts of MTB3A people use. They're never used for advertising, and no one but PostHog, which processes them for us, receives them.

errorReports.title: Error reports
errorReports.body: When something breaks, we want to know before you have to tell us. An error report says where in our code the problem happened, which version you were using, your language, and your device's operating system, browser, and model. Before a report is sent, we remove amounts, names, notes, contact details, request contents, your IP address, and anything you type. When the iPhone or Android app itself crashes, Sentry's own scrubbing removes them instead, because the app can't edit that report first. If a report includes an account at all, it is a random internal ID. Reports are stored by Sentry in the EU. Our servers send a report when a request fails on our side, and the hosted portal sends one when a page crashes in your browser. Our website sends a report when one of its pages crashes or hits an error. The website's reports include no account at all. The iPhone and Android apps send a report when the app crashes or hits an error it can't recover from, and so do the iPhone app's share extension, widgets and Siri shortcuts. They never attach screenshots or what's on your screen.

mobileDeletion.title: Deleting your account and data
mobileDeletion.body: You can delete individual entries at any time. To delete your whole account, choose Close my account: in the web portal under You › Account, or in the iPhone and Android apps on the Account tab. For 30 days you can sign in and keep your account; after that, we delete it. A business profile you share with someone who also owns it passes to them. If other people work in it and none of them is an owner, make one of them an owner, or remove them, before you close your account. We delete your account, the profiles you own with every record and receipt in them, your sign-ins and passkeys, the record that you accepted our terms, and your customer record at Stripe. On profiles that stay because you didn't own them, the records you added stay, without your name. We keep: in those profiles' history, a note that a removed account (a random internal ID, never your name or email) was deleted; at Stripe, the invoices for what you paid, which tax law requires us to keep; your address on our do-not-email list, if you asked us to stop emailing it; for up to 30 days, our email log and our servers' logs, which hold the internal ID or a scrambled form of your address; error reports with the internal ID, until Sentry's retention ends; Resend's records of the emails we sent you; and, if you sent our website's request form or wrote to us, your message, until we delete it within 12 months. Deleted receipt files can be recovered for 14 days, and copies in our backups clear 14 days after deletion. Signing out of the mobile app ends your session. On iPhone, the app's sign-in record can stay in the Keychain until you reinstall the app. Copies of the app's data in iCloud or Google backups made before version 0.1.13 can remain until those backups are replaced.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.body: MTB3A is a business tool and isn't directed at children. We don't knowingly collect information from anyone under 13.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If this policy changes, we'll update this page and the "Last updated" date above.

hostedRequest.title: When you ask for an account
hostedRequest.body: If you send the request form on our website, Netlify, which hosts the website, receives what you type: your name, your email and anything else you choose to add, plus the language the page was in and a random request number. Netlify also records technical details such as your IP address and browser, and checks the request for spam with Akismet. Netlify then emails it to us. We use it only to reply with an offer and, if you go ahead, to set up your account. We delete requests within 12 months; write to info@mtb3a.com and we'll delete yours sooner.
